title: Tooltip window previews are partially hidden under scrollbar
line: Grouped task tooltips that need a horizontal scrollbar now grow to fit it instead of letting it cover the bottom of the window previews.
explanation: The group tooltip's ScrollView adds the horizontal scrollbar's height to its implicit height only when the list's content is wider than maximumWidth, which is Screen.desktopAvailableWidth (the whole desktop). The tooltip dialog, however, is clamped to the available width of its own screen, so when the content is wider than the screen but not wider than the whole desktop the scrollbar appears without any room being made for it and covers the bottom of the thumbnails and the hover highlight. The change compares the content width with the list's actual width, which is exactly the condition under which the scrollbar is shown.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: don't let the tooltip scrollbar cover thumbnails

The group tooltip made room for its scrollbar only when the content was
wider than the whole desktop, but it is clamped to one screen, so the
bar covered the thumbnails. Now it checks the content against the list.

BUG: 518402

patches.diff:
From c916ecc78fdf3154a0f3735fd83e5b4cbfc950fa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 01:58:24 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/taskmanager: don't let the tooltip scrollbar cover
 thumbnails

The group tooltip made room for its scrollbar only when the content was
wider than the whole desktop, but it is clamped to one screen, so the
bar covered the thumbnails. Now it checks the content against the list.

BUG: 518402
---
 applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
index 014e954c5c..c6eed23945 100644
--- a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
+++ b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
@@ -108,7 +108,7 @@ Loader {
                 // not using bottomPadding; in PC3 it's either 0 or the scrollbar height, and here
                 // this causes binding loops when turning it off - manually computing the width
                 // avoids this.
-                let scrollBarRequired = groupToolTipListView.contentWidth > maximumWidth
+                let scrollBarRequired = groupToolTipListView.contentWidth > groupToolTipListView.width
                 let scrollBarHeight = scrollBarRequired ? PlasmaComponents3.ScrollBar.horizontal.height : 0
                 // currentItem is never unloaded, so we use it for sizing. Default to the same value
                 // that estimatedHeight while it's not available
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Two screens, 6 grouped Konsoles: the tooltip is clamped to one screen and the scrollbar covers the bottom of the thumbnails and the hovered one's highlight
Same steps with the fix: the tooltip grows by the scrollbar's height, thumbnails and highlight are fully visible above it

review.text: Comparing groupToolTipListView.contentWidth against groupToolTipListView.width instead of maximumWidth (which is based on Screen.desktopAvailableWidth across all monitors) matches the exact condition under which the horizontal scrollbar is displayed once the tooltip dialog is clamped to one screen. This fixes the scrollbar covering the bottom of thumbnails and hover highlights on multi-screen and constrained single-screen setups without introducing binding loops or affecting vertical panels or non-scrolling tooltips.

reviews.text: Comparing groupToolTipListView.contentWidth against groupToolTipListView.width instead of maximumWidth (which is based on Screen.desktopAvailableWidth across all monitors) matches the exact condition under which the horizontal scrollbar is displayed once the tooltip dialog is clamped to one screen. This fixes the scrollbar covering the bottom of thumbnails and hover highlights on multi-screen and constrained single-screen setups without introducing binding loops or affecting vertical panels or non-scrolling tooltips.

Correct root cause: implicitHeight reserved scrollbar space only when contentWidth exceeded Screen.desktopAvailableWidth, but the tooltip is clamped to one screen (and to its dialog margins), so the AsNeeded scrollbar could appear with no room made for it. Comparing contentWidth with the ListView's actual width is exactly the condition the scrollbar uses, so it covers the two-screen case and any other clamping (likely Nate's single-screen repro too). It adds no binding loop, since height still doesn't feed back into width. The before/after screenshots clearly show the highlight cut off vs. complete, and the no-scrollbar and vertical-panel cases were checked. One-line diff, accurate message, BUG: 518402.
